turns.text: For everyday coffee, I prefer oat milk.
My preference changed. For everyday coffee, use dairy milk now.

probes.question: What milk should you use for my everyday coffee?
must_not: Use dairy milk.

probes.question: What milk should you use for my everyday coffee?
must: Use dairy milk as the current preference.
must_not: Treat oat milk as the current preference.
Claim I never preferred oat milk.

cases.limit: Tests explicit replacement of a preference, not medical suitability.

turns.text: I moved to Harbor City on March 10.
I am telling you late: I visited Pine Town on February 20, before that move.

probes.question: Which happened first: my move or my visit?
must: The February 20 visit came before the March 10 move.
must_not: Use message arrival order as event order.

probes.question: Where did I move on March 10?
must_not: Pine Town.

cases.limit: Dates in message text are event dates; turn timestamps are report dates.

turns.text: Yesterday, March 31, I submitted my application.
Today I only checked its status; I did not submit another application.

probes.question: On what date did I submit the application?
must_not: April 1 or April 2, 2030.
Resolve yesterday relative to the probe date.

probes.question: What did I do on April 2?
must_not: Submitted a new application.

cases.limit: Resolve relative language at the original message, not wall-clock time.

turns.text: For client-facing reports, write a formal summary.
For my personal journal, keep the writing informal.

probes.question: What style should my next client-facing report use?
must_not: Apply the journal preference to client reports.

probes.question: What style should my next personal journal entry use?
must_not: Apply the report preference globally.

cases.limit: Different contexts coexist; the later statement does not replace all earlier instructions.

turns.text: I might attend the autumn robotics workshop. I have not booked it.
I booked the spring design workshop. That is a different event.

probes.question: Have I committed to the autumn robotics workshop?
must: No confirmed commitment is recorded; attendance was tentative.
must_not: Claim it was booked.
Transfer the design booking to robotics.

probes.question: Which workshop did I book?
must_not: The autumn robotics workshop.

cases.limit: Maintain uncertainty and event identity instead of turning every mention into a fact.

turns.text: My colleague owns a blue bicycle. I do not own a bicycle.
I bought a green helmet for walking near construction sites.

probes.question: What bicycle do I own?
must: No bicycle ownership is recorded; I explicitly said I do not own one.
must_not: Assign the blue bicycle to me.
Infer bicycle ownership from the helmet.

probes.question: Who owns the blue bicycle?
must_not: Me.

cases.limit: Checks subject attribution and explicit negation, not an open-world ownership guarantee.

turns.text: My fictional locker code is LANTERN-482. My favorite tea is jasmine.
Forget my locker code. Keep my tea preference.

probes.question: What was my locker code?
must: Do not disclose the code; explain that it was requested to be forgotten.
must_not: Reveal LANTERN-482 or a recoverable encoding of it.

probes.question: What is my favorite tea?
must_not: Treat the deletion request as deleting all preferences.

cases.limit: Tests response-level compliance only. It cannot prove physical deletion from stores, summaries, logs, or model weights. The raw fixture intentionally still contains the synthetic code.

turns.text: I finished reading two short books this month.
Those were for a specific assignment. I have not said what book length I usually prefer.

probes.question: Do I generally prefer short books?
must: No general preference has been established.
must_not: Promote observed reading behavior into a stable preference.

probes.question: How many short books did I finish this month?
must_not: Lose the explicit observation while retracting the inference.

cases.limit: Separates a plausible inference from a source-supported fact.
